flags.finding: [partially supported] Scene S004 scripts the classic rock song 'Baba O'Riley' blasting from the stereo of Vick's Cadillac convertible as the characters drive down Highway 10. The musical composition was written by Pete Townshend and is published and administered through Fabulous Music Ltd (PRS/BMI), ABKCO Music Inc. (BMI), and Spirit Music Group / Warner Chappell. Synchronizing this protected musical composition to motion picture imagery requires a negotiated synchronization license from all controlling music publishers. Quoted sync licensing fees for iconic top-tier classic rock anthems of this caliber typically range from $35,000 to $75,000+ for worldwide all-media theatrical film rights. Ownership splits must be confirmed via Songview prior to finalizing negotiations.

citations.excerpt: Synchronization License: This is the right to synchronize a song or a piece of music with your visual image. It must be obtained from the copyright owner of the music, which is usually the publisher.

remedy.detail: Negotiate a synchronization license directly with Pete Townshend's co-publishers (ABKCO Music, Fabulous Music / Spirit Music Group, and Warner Chappell Music). For indie budget containment, use the track as an editorial temp cue and replace in the final mix with a pre-cleared indie rock track or commercial music library cue ($1,500–$5,000 licensing fee), avoiding sound-alikes that infringe publicity or arrangement rights. Commercial sync licensing quote: $35,000–$75,000 (fixed licensing fee).

flags.finding: [partially supported] In scene S004, the script calls for The Who's original master recording of 'Baba O'Riley' to be blasted from the convertible's stereo. Master recording fees for marquee legacy rock recordings are negotiated on a Most Favored Nations (MFN) basis with the composition synchronization license, typically commanding $35,000 to $75,000+ for worldwide theatrical and streaming distribution rights.
